correctness.rationale: An independent Gaussian-age renewal reduction at zero coupling is justified by boundedness of the angular ratio. The exact circular contour identity was reconstructed by residues, including the inside/outside threshold. Polar integration gives a signed Bessel-I1 representation, so the finite-rate sign and equality-temperature zero are rigorous. Uniform large-argument I1 asymptotics at the radial endpoint produce the small-age coefficient 8 Tplus^2/(R^3 sqrt(pi DeltaT)); a saddle at age R/(2 sqrt(Tplus r)) gives the sharp exp[-R sqrt(r/Tplus)]/sqrt(r) result and factor exp[R^2/(4 Tplus)]. OU second moments give the contrasting 2 DeltaT/(r+2). Exact numerical reproduction (30 checks) supports the formulas but is not offered as an infinite proof. Fixed positive temperatures and radius, weak-coupling order of limits and omitted reset jumps are explicit.

originality.rationale: The 2026 model source already gives the full renewal propagator and circular-reset angular-velocity integral, and the general reset/OU framework is old. This claim is limited to a newly extracted nonperturbative high-reset susceptibility, all-orders angular erasure identity and exact saddle prefactor. No reviewed source states this singular result or mathematically dominates it with an explicit same-limit expansion. The general integral represents the observable implicitly but requires a new contour cancellation, a Bessel endpoint asymptotic and an age saddle; ordinary substitution or a known moment formula does not provide the stated coefficient. Search nonhits are not novelty proof; unindexed exact asymptotics remain a risk.
residual_risks: The 2026 model paper supplies an exact unevaluated angular-velocity integral; a differently formulated asymptotic could be implicit in it or in another analysis.
Earlier anisotropic reset literature was compared only from accessible abstracts for some items; whole-text coverage cannot be excluded.

value.rationale: This is a physically motivated response coefficient, not a renamed stationary moment. A uniform reset angle erases all interior contributions, leading to an exponentially small weak-coupling angular-velocity response despite an algebraic angular-momentum response; the precise coefficient and sign provide experimentally interpretable sensitivity scales. The rare-event mechanism is structural and distinct from a finite sample or textbook exercise.
